title: Show HN: PDT – Open-source deployment of scheduled jobs on your own cloud

item.text:
Hi, I'm Derek. I've been doing data integrations / ETL work since 2014, first for K-12, now for commercial companies think ADP/BambooHR to AzureAD, etc. I've written so many deployment systems for integrations, each slightly different. Instead, we took the best parts of all the systems we've built and put them into one tool. PDT takes your job and deploys it to AWS, Azure, GCP, or even Task Scheduler. It's a convention-over-configuration deployment tool specifically made for Scheduled Jobs. Things like data integrations, scans, reports, etc.

With AI, writing scripts is easier than ever. Deploying them into production isn't as easy. Because the AI needs to know what you want, this can be tricky as there are so many choices to make! Do I use Azure Functions, Duarble Functions, Container Instances, Azure Batch, AKS CronJob, Azure Automation Runbooks, Logic Apps? ahhh, I just want this to run in production.

To give it a shot, install uv, then:

  uv tool install pdt-cli
  uv tool update-shell
  pdt init jobs
  cd jobs
  pdt run hello-world # runs locally
  pdt deploy hello-world # runs on cloud 
  pdt new hello --from powershell-hello-world # give powershell a shot
PDT gives you a standard set of primitives to use for scheduling, secrets, storage, logs, and alerts. This means you already know how to track state, where to drop the file you wanted to drop, how to know when the job fails, and how to answer all the other orchestration-related questions.
item.title: Show HN: PDT – Open-source deployment of scheduled jobs on your own cloud

sources.text:
pdt - process deploy tool
Turn any script into a scheduled job in your cloud.
pdt builds, runs, and deploys scheduled jobs to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, or Windows Task Scheduler. It gives every job the same
primitives
, chosen from years of deploying scheduled jobs for businesses on each cloud. No servers to run and nothing extra to install, and everything it makes lives in your own account.
Key Features
Bring your scripts
- Drop in your PowerShell or Python files. pdt finds what they need and runs them.
One command to deploy
- No cloud skills needed.
pdt deploy
installs the tools it needs and opens the sign-in page for you.
Any cloud
- Move a job between AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Windows by changing one line.
Know the cost first
- See the plan and a monthly cost estimate before anything changes.
Know when it breaks
- Health checks, logs, a dashboard, and alerts to Slack, Teams, or email.
Quick Start
Windows
Download and run the
pdt installer
.
macOS / Linux - with uv
Install
uv
, then pdt:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
source $HOME/.local/bin/env
uv tool install pdt-cli
uv tool update-shell
For other ways to install, and how to update or remove pdt, see
docs/install.md
.
Deploy your first job
Then run:
pdt init jobs
cd jobs
pdt new hello-powershell --from powershell-hello-world
cd hello-powershell
pdt run
pdt deploy
pdt logs
Deploy your own script
Create the job with
pdt new your-powershell-job --from powershell-hello-world
Replace
hello.ps1
in the
your-powershell-job
folder with your own
.ps1
script
Test the job locally with
pdt run your-powershell-job
Deploy it with
pdt deploy your-powershell-job
See
every command
.
Example deployment
A first deploy of the
hello-world-example
app to Azure, then a look at its run:
See
the same output as text
.
The bundled examples
Run
pdt examples
to list them, then
pdt new <name> --from <example>
to copy one.
hello-world
Small job that logs "Hello world."
pdt init
puts a copy of this in every new empty project.
azure-license-waste
PowerShell job. Finds the Microsoft 365 licenses a tenant pays for that nobody uses: paid licenses on disabled accounts, on accounts that have not signed in for 90 days (or never did), and seats bought but assigned to nobody. Each run keeps a
LicenseWaste-<date>.xlsx
workbook in the job's data store, with a Summary sheet of monthly and annual cost and one sheet per finding.
impossible-travel-report
Looks at recent Entra ID sign-ins. Sends an email when one person signs in from two far-apart places too quickly: Dallas an hour ago, Paris now.
Settings for the lookback window, the minimum distance, and the email addresses live in the job's
config.yml
. The env vars it needs are listed there too, and in its
env.template
.
intune-export
PowerShell job. Once a week it exports the Intune configuration of a tenant with the bulk export of
IntuneManagement
version 4, and keeps an
IntuneExport-<date>.zip
in the job's data store. To import, unzip it and point IntuneManagement's import at the company folder inside.
monday-orphaned-account-report
Reports active Monday users whose email address does not match the
userPrincipalName
of an active Entra ID user.
powershell-hello-world
A PowerShell job whose one script,
hello.ps1
, writes "Hello, world!". It is the job the
Quick Start
deploys. Put your own
.ps1
files in its folder in place of
hello.ps1
to deploy your own PowerShell job.
powershell-report
PowerShell job. small CSV report with
Export-Csv
, and pdt keeps the file in the app's data store.
Support
AutoIDM
makes pdt. Any issues, questions, ideas, or concerns? Use any of these methods to get a hold of us:
Discord
Report a problem at
https://github.com/AutoIDM/pdt/issues
.
Documentation
How pdt works
: the building blocks every job gets on each cloud, and the practices behind them
Projects and apps
: set up a project, add an app, and where pdt keeps its files
Deploying
: deploy, run, pause, and destroy a job, and run pdt from CI
Commands
: every
pdt
command and its options
Choosing where jobs run
: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Windows Task Scheduler, and your own Dockerfile
Keeping files between runs
: the storage folder every app gets, and state that carries from one run to the next
The dashboard
:
pdt gui
, the browser view of every app's runs, logs, and files
Writing your own app
: Python and PowerShell apps, and logging
Sending email
: send mail from an app over SMTP, Microsoft Graph, SES, or Resend
More ways to install
: other installs, and how to update or remove pdt
